about.title: Sebastopol Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Sebastopol is a small city, but its residents rely on the same manufactured goods — vehicles, tools, appliances, farm equipment, children's products — as anywhere else in Sonoma County, and any of them can fail in ways that cause real harm. California law gives injured people an advantage here: product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, meaning you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That covers design flaws, manufacturing errors, and inadequate warnings alike, and liability can extend to the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer who put the product into the stream of commerce. If a defective product injured you along Rt 116, Bodega Avenue, Rt 12, Petaluma Avenue, or anywhere else in Sebastopol, we can review what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you generally don't need to prove the maker was negligent — just that the defect existed and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may give you more than one avenue toward accountability.

items.title: Evidence Matters — Especially the Product Itself
items.desc: We can advise you early on preserving the defective product intact, since it's often the most important piece of evidence in these claims.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm, not on how careful or careless the manufacturer was. We can review your specific situation to confirm which legal theory applies.

items.question: I still have the product that hurt me — what should I do with it?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't repair, alter, or throw it away, since it's often central evidence in a product liability claim. We can advise you on proper storage and documentation.

items.question: Does this apply if the defective product was bought outside Sebastopol?
items.answer: Yes. What matters is where the injury happened and where you live, not necessarily where the product was purchased. If you were injured in Sebastopol or elsewhere in Sonoma County, we can discuss your options.
